member.summary: Cross-file semantic checks (03 §8) that attributes can't express: sums, membership, consistency.

member.name: M:SeatOfPower.Sim.Content.ContentChecks.Color
member.remarks:
Pattern:
^#[0-9A-Fa-f]{6}$
Explanation:
○ Match if at the beginning of the string.
○ Match '#'.
○ Match a hexadecimal digit exactly 6 times.
○ Match if at the end of the string or if before an ending newline.

member.name: M:SeatOfPower.Sim.Content.ContentChecks.ThreeUpper
member.remarks:
Pattern:
^[A-Z]{3}$
Explanation:
○ Match if at the beginning of the string.
○ Match a character in the set [A-Z] exactly 3 times.
○ Match if at the end of the string or if before an ending newline.

member.name: M:SeatOfPower.Sim.Content.ContentChecks.VariablePattern
member.remarks:
Pattern:
^[a-z0-9_]+(\\.[a-z0-9_]+)*(@(\\{country\\}|[a-z0-9_]+(\\.[a-z0-9_]+)*))?$
Explanation:
○ Match if at the beginning of the string.
○ Match a character in the set [0-9_a-z] greedily at least once.
○ Loop greedily any number of times.
○ 1st capture group.
○ Match '.'.
○ Match a character in the set [0-9_a-z] greedily at least once.
○ Optional (greedy).
○ 2nd capture group.
○ Match '@'.
○ 3rd capture group.
○ Match with 2 alternative expressions.
○ Match the string "{country}".
○ Match a sequence of expressions.
○ Match a character in the set [0-9_a-z] greedily at least once.
○ Loop greedily any number of times.
○ 4th capture group.
○ Match '.'.
○ Match a character in the set [0-9_a-z] atomically at least once.
○ Match if at the end of the string or if before an ending newline.

Strict: unknown files and properties, missing required fields, bad enum names, unresolved ids, out-of-range numbers and missing localisation keys are errors. All errors are collected and reported together, each with its file and JSON path.

remarks.para: Layout (03 §2): sources/sources.json, variables/*.json, economy/default_params.json, world/commodities.json, countries/<code>/{country, economy_start, economy_params, power_centers, legislature, voter_blocs, characters, relations}.json, policies/*.json, events/*.json, decision_points/*.json, considerations/*.json, roles/*.json, justifications/*.json, verbs/*.json, chains/*.json, legality/*.json, procedures/*.json, dialogue/en/*.json, localization/en/*.json, scenarios/<name>/scenario.json and generated/**. schemas/ and non-JSON files are ignored.

Layering: any JSON value may be {"$ref": "generated:<key>"}, replaced by the generated value. If the generated value is an object, sibling properties next to $ref override its fields. Provenance is recorded.

member.name: M:SeatOfPower.Sim.Content.ContentValidator.PlainKey
member.remarks:
Pattern:
^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*$
Explanation:
○ Match if at the beginning of the string.
○ Match a character in the set [A-Z_a-z].
○ Match a character in the set [0-9A-Z_a-z] atomically any number of times.
○ Match if at the end of the string or if before an ending newline.

member.name: M:SeatOfPower.Sim.Content.ContentValidator.IdBody
member.remarks:
Pattern:
^[a-z0-9_]+(\\.[a-z0-9_]+)*$
Explanation:
○ Match if at the beginning of the string.
○ Match a character in the set [0-9_a-z] greedily at least once.
○ Loop greedily any number of times.
○ 1st capture group.
○ Match '.'.
○ Match a character in the set [0-9_a-z] atomically at least once.
○ Match if at the end of the string or if before an ending newline.

member.name: T:SeatOfPower.Sim.Content.ConsiderationDef
member.summary: A reusable consideration from the shared library (07 §3.2): one input, mapped through a response curve to a score. File: data/considerations/*.json.
member.param: Input id: trait.<name> (the actor's personality, 0–1), an input supplied by the decision's code (e.g. order.lawfulness), or one registered by a package through SimServices.RegisterUtilityInput.
How the input becomes a score.
Weight in the option's weighted geometric mean.
A trait that scales the weight by 0.5 + trait / 100 (so 0 halves it and 100 makes it 1.5×), e.g. lawfulness for legal considerations.
Input value used when nothing provides the input (keeps packages that aren't built yet neutral).

When nothing provides the input, leave the consideration out instead of scoring : for situational considerations (e.g. a missed deadline on a must-pass bill) that must not dilute the mean of every other case.

member.name: T:SeatOfPower.Sim.Content.DealTermDef
member.summary: A term of a diplomatic deal (08 §4): data/diplomacy/terms.json. A term is given by one country (the giver) to another (the receiver) at a size (token 0.4, limited 1, major 2). What it is worth to each side is computed in code from the value factors below, read against both countries' economies, pressures, goals and leaders, so one term list serves every country pair. Scripts see the giver as {country} and the receiver as {target}.
member.param: What giving it is worth to the giver (usually a cost), in value points at limited size.
What receiving it is worth to the receiver, in value points at limited size.
Power center stakes it hits in the giver's country (full countries): stake → loyalty change per 100 points of stake at limited size, e.g. a tariff cut costs manufacturing lobbies.
Power center stakes it helps or hurts in the receiver's country.
True if it is a promise kept over time (a holding pledge, a truce on tariffs) rather than something delivered at once; accepting someone's pledge takes trust in them.
True for face-saving terms (a joint statement, a summit) a counter-offer may add.
When it can be part of a deal (06 condition), e.g. sanctions relief needs sanctions.
06 effects when the agreement starts, scaled by the term's size.
06 condition checked weekly while in force: true means the giver broke it.
06 condition: true means keeping it has become costly for the giver, who then weighs honouring it.
How long it lasts (0: until revoked).
Days before the same giver can give the same receiver this term again.

member.name: T:SeatOfPower.Sim.Content.ReactionDef
member.summary: A reaction an affected actor can choose (07 §7): data/reactions/*.json. Each reaction is the option of dp.react_to_action with the id after reaction.; the decision point holds its considerations, this holds who may use it and what it does.
member.param: Actor kinds that may choose it.
Toward the leader: −1 strong support … +1 strong opposition.
Personal cost or risk to the actor, 0–1.
How big a response it is, 0–1 (matched to how hard the act hit the actor).
Minimum affectedness for it to be an option.
The act must not be public yet (leaks, whistleblowing).
The act must come from an order (e.g. suing over it).
Only the act's target (or its power center) may choose it.
The root act must have done something (an order carried out, a firing, a policy or law), not merely been attempted: there is nothing to sue over or defund otherwise.
The root act must be at least this unlawful (no lawsuits or criminal referrals over lawful acts).
Only actors still in office (not those who resigned or were fired).
Only people with first-hand knowledge: those in the order's chain or involved in the incident, the target, or security and military leaders when it is their field (leaks, memos, whistleblowing).
same: only actors of the leader's party; opposition: only other parties; null: any.
If set, the act kinds it applies to.
Extra 06 effects (country and character set to the actor's).
An 06 condition that must hold (character set to the actor's).
True if others react to it in turn (an act at depth + 1).
Severity of the act it becomes.
For foreign actors (08): rival (only leaders whose opinion of the act's country is below −20) or partner (only those at 0 or above); null: any.

member.name: T:SeatOfPower.Sim.Content.VerbDef
member.summary: A verb of the action composer (23 §3.1): what the player orders. File: data/verbs/*.json. An order is a verb, a target, a method and the shared parameters (scale, secrecy, justification). Verbs are generic across countries; the method names an executor kind, and each country's for that kind says who carries it out.
member.param: Ways to carry it out (at least one).
Target kinds it accepts (empty: no target).
For power-center targets: allowed types (empty: any).
For character targets: allowed CharacterDef.Role values (empty: any).
Legality when no legality rule matches.
Political capital it costs to issue.
Days before the same verb can be ordered against the same target again.
Condition for it to be available (06 language).
Effects when the order is carried out (scaled by the order's scale).
Effects when the order is stopped (refused or void).
True to ask the player for one confirmation in the UI (never disabled, D-019).
What an order of this verb is for, as a check the UI makes while the order is in flight (D-028); null: it always serves its purpose.

member.name: T:SeatOfPower.Sim.Content.VerbPurposeDef

Slow chains can carry an order out after its reason has gone (playtest 2: prioritisation executed a week after Congress fixed the limit), so the Orders screen warns while the check fails and the player can withdraw. The simulation never reads it: orders don't lapse on their own.

member.name: M:SeatOfPower.Sim.Content.Scripting.ScriptCompiler.FlagPattern
member.remarks:
Pattern:
^[a-z0-9_{}]+(\\.[a-z0-9_{}]+)*$
Explanation:
○ Match if at the beginning of the string.
○ Match a character in the set [0-9_a-{}] greedily at least once.
○ Loop greedily any number of times.
○ 1st capture group.
○ Match '.'.
○ Match a character in the set [0-9_a-{}] atomically at least once.
○ Match if at the end of the string or if before an ending newline.

member.name: T:SeatOfPower.Sim.Core.Modifier
member.summary: A timed effect on a variable ("raises growth by 0.3 pp starting in 6 months"). Modifiers are an overlay: the store's visible value is (base + Σ additive) × Π(1 + multiplicative), and each active modifier appears in the target's ledger, sourced to . Systems own the base; modifiers are never baked into it, so they expire cleanly.
member.remarks: A system that integrates its variable over time (e.g. with ) should not let modifiers target that state variable directly, or it would see them twice. Point modifiers at a separate input variable instead (e.g. econ.gap_shock@country.usa, base 0) and read it as a term.

member.name: T:SeatOfPower.Sim.Core.VariableStore
member.summary: Every gameplay quantity the player can see, with a contribution ledger explaining each update (02 §6) and history for charts.

remarks.para: Each variable has a base owned by systems (, ) plus a modifier overlay. returns clamp((base + Σ additive) × Π(1 + multiplicative)).
Contributions recorded during a tick are turned into an immutable at rollover (tick step 5), together with the modifiers' share. A variable nothing touched keeps its previous ledger.
Mutate variables only inside a tick (systems, commands, decision handlers) or during system initialisation; contributions recorded between ticks are not saved.

member.name: T:SeatOfPower.Sim.Dialogue.DialogueEngine
member.summary: Deterministic line selection (10 §3). Filter the template's lines by condition and tone (with fallbacks), prefer the speaker's voices (generic lines are the fallback), avoid lines the speaker used in the last days and lines anyone used in the last days (five allies backing the President on one day, two outlets with the same slant), then pick by weight with the speaker's dialogue stream. records the choice (sim thread only); picks by hash and changes nothing (UI tooltips, the composer's preview).

member.name: P:SeatOfPower.Sim.Dialogue.DialogueSurfaces.CommonVariables
member.summary: Variables every line may use: the speaker's name and country, the player's leader, how the speaker addresses them (counterpart_title, e.g. "President Ashdown"), the player's country, and the player's party and the opposition as adjectives (own_party, opp_party: "Democratic") and as members (own_party_members, opp_party_members: "Democrats"). Never write a party's name in a line (D-013): lines must read fairly whichever party the player leads.

member.name: T:SeatOfPower.Sim.Dialogue.DialogueSystem
member.summary: Dialogue (10), at . Lines are chosen when a tick's events are handed out: the system registers , which gives each event its lines (negotiation replies, statements, briefings, headlines...) and records them in the saved log. Weekly it forgets line uses older than . Forecast clones don't speak.

member.name: T:SeatOfPower.Sim.SimHost
member.summary: Runs a on a dedicated background thread (01 §4). Other threads send commands with and read and events; nothing else touches the simulation.

remarks.para: Each loop: drain inbox → tick → hand new decision requests to the resolver → publish snapshot and events → auto-pause and autosave → wait for the speed's real-time delay.
When the tick blocks on a decision, the host retries as answers arrive and, after , queues the utility fallback ().
Once the thread stops (a fault or ), work still queued fails and new saves, queries and forecasts fail at once, so no caller waits forever.

member.summary: The leader's cabinet (09 §9): who holds each post, hiring and firing, departures, influence, leaks and resignations. member.name: T:SeatOfPower.Sim.Systems.Advisors.OrderAdvice
member.summary: Advisors' predictions of who in an order's chain will balk (09 §9): 23's chain preview seen through each advisor's competence (noise) and bias. Hawks underrate refusals of force, loyal yes-men underrate refusals of anything the boss wants, and alarmists overrate them. Pure: the noise is a hash of advisor, order and day, so asking twice on a day gives the same answer and nothing in the game changes.

member.name: T:SeatOfPower.Sim.Systems.Advisors.RecommendationService
member.summary: Advisors' recommendations (09 §9). When the player faces an event, a crisis stage or a drafted bill, the advisors whose fields it touches each value every option through their own goals (data/advisors/goals.json), their faction, their appetite for risk and what the boss's voters would like, then choose what to push through dp.advisor_recommendation (so they disagree visibly and not always predictably). Each recommendation carries its strength, how alarmist its framing is and the ledger causes it cites. When the player chooses, followed advisors gain influence; overruled ones lose some, and their factions resent it more the more the winner's influence has grown.

member.name: T:SeatOfPower.Sim.Systems.Behaviour.ImpactModel
member.summary: Who an act concerns and which side they take (07 §7). Affectedness combines being the target or its ally, the actor's domain (officers care about military acts, prosecutors about justice), the act's gravity weighed by the actor's lawfulness, policy distance, and visibility (until an act is public only insiders know). Stance combines harm, unlawfulness, policy distance, partisanship, loyalty and grievance; for reactions to reactions, the root act's character plus the credibility of whoever spoke out.

member.summary: Reactions to acts (07 §7). Consequences land after the reaction's delay; a cascading reaction becomes an act at depth + 1, up to .

member.name: T:SeatOfPower.Sim.Systems.Diplomacy.CounterOffers
member.summary:
Generates counter-offers and NPC proposals in code (08 §4), from what terms are worth to each side:
Ask for more (counter_A): a bigger share of the term they value most, or a term they want that is cheap for the other side.
Save face (counter_B): drop or shrink the term that costs them most, drop red lines, and (for proud leaders) add a symbolic term both sides can show at home.
Propose: what a leader asks for when seeking a deal, and what they offer in return.
Red-line terms never appear in anything a leader proposes.

member.name: F:SeatOfPower.Sim.Systems.Diplomacy.CounterOffers.MaxTerms
member.summary: Most terms a deal may have.

member.summary: The terms of a deal that cross the responder's red lines.

member.summary: True if a term crosses one of the country's red lines.
member.param: The country whose red lines apply.

member.name: M:SeatOfPower.Sim.Systems.Diplomacy.CounterOffers.AskMore(SeatOfPower.Sim.Content.Scripting.ScriptContext@,System.Collections.Generic.IReadOnlyList{SeatOfPower.Sim.Systems.Diplomacy.DealTerm},System.String,System.String)
member.summary: The responder's "ask for more" counter: a bigger version of a term they receive, or an extra term they want from the proposer, chosen for what it gains them plus half what it costs the proposer (they ask for what the other side might grant). Null if nothing gains them at least 3 points.

member.name: M:SeatOfPower.Sim.Systems.Diplomacy.CounterOffers.SaveFace(SeatOfPower.Sim.Content.Scripting.ScriptContext,System.Collections.Generic.IReadOnlyList{SeatOfPower.Sim.Systems.Diplomacy.DealTerm},System.String,System.String)
member.summary: The responder's "save face" counter: red lines dropped, the term that costs them most shrunk (or dropped from token), and for a proud leader a symbolic term added. Null if that changes nothing or leaves them nothing worth signing.

member.name: M:SeatOfPower.Sim.Systems.Diplomacy.CounterOffers.Propose(SeatOfPower.Sim.Content.Scripting.ScriptContext@,System.String,System.String,System.Boolean)
member.summary: What a leader proposes when seeking a deal (dp.weekly_stance = seek_deal): the term they want most from the other side (worth at least 6 to them), plus — unless it is a demand — the term they could give that is worth most to the other side for what it costs them, as long as the deal still gains them 3 or more. Null if they want nothing.
member.param: True for a demand (nothing offered in return).

member.summary: What a leader offers in return for : the term they can give that is worth most to the other side for what it costs them, as long as the whole deal still gains them ; null if none qualifies.
member.param: Least the deal must be worth to them.

member.summary: True if a term may be proposed by or to : allowed now, off cooldown, and over nobody's red line.

member.name: T:SeatOfPower.Sim.Systems.Diplomacy.CreditorService
member.summary: Foreign creditors (08 §6, dp.treasury_holdings_action): governments that control large holdings of another country's debt decide monthly, and again right after a shock (missed payments, a default, the X-date, a downgrade), whether to hold, quietly reduce, publicly reduce, or buy as leverage. Reductions push the debtor's term premium up through 04's econ.foreign_demand_shift; a public sale also signals and spikes market stress. Inputs: default risk, brinkmanship, market stress, opinion, trust, rivalry, the creditor's own exposure (dumping hurts the seller too), a holding pledge, provocation, its liquidity needs and reassurance on debt.

member.name: T:SeatOfPower.Sim.Systems.Diplomacy.DiplomacySystem
member.summary: Diplomacy and foreign leaders (08), at . Daily: agreements are checked for broken terms; orders, incidents and economic milestones that touch other countries become memories, world events and creditor reviews; negotiations lapse; creditors due for an early review decide. Weekly (Mondays): relations and dependence are recomputed, agreements are checked (expiry, violations, honouring), foreign leaders choose their stance toward the player. Monthly: creditors and oil producers decide.
member.remarks: Registers the 06 relation effect, the RelationQuery condition service, 07's foreign hooks (ForeignReactors, ForeignImpact, RelationShift), 04's TariffResponse (trade disputes) and the handlers of the scheduled diplomacy decision points. Relations, dependence, deals and treaties are generic across country pairs, so 21 can extend them.

member.name: T:SeatOfPower.Sim.Systems.Diplomacy.ForeignAffairs
member.summary:
How the world abroad sees a country's acts (08 §5):
Orders that touch another country (sanctions, tariffs, strikes, messages) leave its leader a memory, sized by the verb's relation impact (or derived from its effect, severity and category), its scale and the leader's pride.
Economic milestones (missed payments, a default, the X-date, a downgrade) hit creditors' trust and become world events foreign leaders comment on, and send creditors to review their holdings.
Foreign leaders react to acts through 07's dp.react_to_action: who cares is decided by interest (being the target, alliances, rivalry, dependence, the act's field), and which side they take by harm, opinion, unlawfulness, alliances and how much they depend on the actor.

member.name: T:SeatOfPower.Sim.Systems.Diplomacy.NegotiationService
member.summary: Deals and negotiation (08 §4). An offer is answered after the counterpart deliberates; a session (a modal in the UI, the game pauses) runs up to a few rounds where each proposal is answered at once and the counterpart's patience and face visibly matter. Answers come from dp.respond_to_offer (accept, reject, ask for more, save face, stall); counters are generated in code (); red-line terms are never accepted. After answering, the counterpart may leak the talks (dp.leak_negotiation). Leaders also propose deals and make demands themselves (weekly stance), and ask to renegotiate agreements that have become costly.

member.name: T:SeatOfPower.Sim.Systems.Diplomacy.OilService
member.summary: Oil producers' output (08 §6, dp.oil_output): monthly, a producer cuts, holds, raises or raises sharply. Inputs: the oil price against its fiscal breakeven, fear of losing market share when prices are very high, an output commitment in force, friendly requests from consumers (weighed by opinion), public pressure (which a proud leader resents), and its own fiscal and economic pressure. The choice moves world.oil_price for a few months (a supply shock on 04's oil model).

member.summary: Foreign leaders' weekly stance toward the player's country (08 §5, dp.weekly_stance): warm up, hold, cool, pressure (a demand), or seek a deal (their own proposal). Inputs: opinion, trust, threat, dependence, the recent trend, how weak the other side looks, what they want from it, domestic pressure and a weak economy. The stance also colours how they answer offers. 21 extends the same decision to each leader's top partners (AI-to-AI); here every leader faces the player.

member.name: T:SeatOfPower.Sim.Systems.Economy.EconomySystem
member.summary: The central bank (04 §4, 07 §9): the rate changes only at scheduled meetings, in 25 bp steps. The Taylor rule is computed in code; the choice among −50/−25/0/+25/+50 is dp.central_bank_rate, scored by the 07 utility AI with the chair's personality (patience sets gradualism, hawkishness the weight on inflation) and independence versus political pressure.

The economy (04): a small New Keynesian core per fully simulated country (IS curve, Phillips curve, Okun's law) run weekly, with fiscal and debt, energy, currency, trade, confidence and inequality blocks; daily markets (yields, risk premium, stress, stocks); the US Treasury's daily cash, debt limit, extraordinary measures and X-date; default and shutdown consequences; light countries and a world block. Central bank rate decisions (dp.central_bank_rate) and rating actions (dp.rating_action) go through the NPC AI (07). Every variable it sets carries ledger terms that add up to the value or change.
member.remarks: Variables are owned as base + modifier overlay (02 §7): the system integrates the base, and policies, events and orders may put modifiers on most economy variables (inflation, gas price, oil, confidence, stress, potential growth, revenue share, ...), which then feed every equation that reads them. Shock inputs (econ.gap_shock, econ.risk_premium_shock, econ.foreign_demand_shift, econ.treasury_receipts_factor) exist for content that wants to push a term rather than a level.
member.summary: The weekly macro core of a fully simulated country (04 §4).
Daily markets (04 §4): risk and term premia, the 10-year yield, market stress and the stock index.
Player levers handled by the economy (04 §8): budget effects, bill provisions, tariffs and sanctions.

Sovereign ratings (04 §5, 07 §9): each fictional agency reviews each fully simulated country on its own schedule and when something big happens (missed payments, an X-date within weeks, fundamentals far from the rating). The review is dp.rating_action: the agency compares its rating with a "fair" rating computed from fiscal metrics and political risk, and decides after its own lag.
Starting values: seeding from content, scenario overrides and calibration of reference levels.

The US Treasury's daily cash (04 §5): receipts and outlays from the daily profile scaled by the macro budget, borrowing up to the debt limit plus extraordinary measures, the X-date projection, missed payments (default) and government shutdowns.
The world block (oil, world aggregates) and light countries (04 §6).

member.param: Day 0 (the outlook's arrays start the day after).

End of a suspension, or null.
Room when a suspension ends: the normal cash balance plus fresh extraordinary measures (bn).
Whether day i + 1 is a federal business day (flows are booked then).
Whether day i + 1 is in the April tax season.
Relative daily noise of receipts (outlays have half of it).
Booked months, oldest first (the current month last, incomplete).

member.summary: Runs every clone to the last quarter's end and summarises them. Clones run in parallel; the result does not depend on scheduling.

member.name: T:SeatOfPower.Sim.Systems.Intel.ForecastService
member.summary: Economic forecasts (09 §7): N clones of the game run forward 4–8 quarters, each with perturbed coefficients (model uncertainty) and its own random shocks (the clones never see the real future's draws), holding the current policy (and, by default, politics) fixed or applying the player's proposal. The result is the median and 50%/90% bands of growth, inflation, unemployment, the deficit and the 10-year yield. Clones are made on the sim thread and run on any thread; they never touch the real game. Advisors present the result through their lens ().

member.name: P:SeatOfPower.Sim.Systems.Intel.ForecastService.EconomicSystems
member.summary: The systems an economic forecast runs: the economy and the policies in force (politics is held fixed).

member.name: P:SeatOfPower.Sim.Systems.Intel.ForecastService.Variables
member.summary: The variables forecast, and which direction is good news.

member.name: M:SeatOfPower.Sim.Systems.Intel.ForecastService.Prepare(SeatOfPower.Sim.Simulation,SeatOfPower.Sim.Systems.Intel.ForecastRequest)
member.summary: Makes the clones (call on the sim thread, between ticks).

member.name: M:SeatOfPower.Sim.Systems.Intel.ForecastService.Run(SeatOfPower.Sim.Simulation,SeatOfPower.Sim.Systems.Intel.ForecastRequest)
member.summary: Prepares and runs a forecast synchronously.

member.name: M:SeatOfPower.Sim.Systems.Intel.ForecastService.RunAsync(SeatOfPower.Sim.Simulation,SeatOfPower.Sim.Systems.Intel.ForecastRequest)
member.summary: Prepares the clones now (sim thread) and runs them on the thread pool.

member.name: T:SeatOfPower.Sim.Systems.Intel.PollService
member.summary: Polls and the polling average (09 §4). Each firm polls on its own schedule: the true approval of each voter bloc in the middle of its fieldwork, misread by the firm's blind spots, weighted by population, plus its partisan house effect (which favours one party, so its sign depends on the leader's) and sampling noise. The average weights polls by recency, size and quality, estimates each firm's house effect against the average and takes it out.

member.name: T:SeatOfPower.Sim.Systems.Intel.ReportService
member.summary: Foreign intelligence (09 §8). Routine reports on each foreign country read its leader's next likely move (what to do with the player's debt, oil output, the stance toward the player) or a domestic weakness. Each samples the truth with an accuracy set by the intelligence chief's competence and the target's opacity, may describe an older situation, and states a confidence that an overconfident agency inflates. Insight from intelligence work and diplomacy uncovers hidden red lines and pressures once it passes a threshold drawn for each item.

member.name: T:SeatOfPower.Sim.Systems.Intel.StatisticsService
member.summary: Official statistics (09 §3). Each day it adds the day's true values to the open periods of every series; when a period's release day comes, it publishes the first estimate (truth plus noise), schedules revisions whose errors shrink and stay correlated with the earlier ones (so revisions converge), and updates the perceived value of the variable the series measures. Treasury statements come from the economy's booked months; daily statements are exact with a one-day lag.

member.name: T:SeatOfPower.Sim.Systems.Intel.WhipService
member.summary: Whip counts (09 §6). The Legislative Affairs Director reads each bloc from its announced or likely stance and each swing member from what they say. Members are contacted in turn (the more competent the director, the more per count); a member who won't vote yes may promise to anyway, more often the less honest they are (they tell the White House what it wants to hear), the director's reading has noise by their competence, and readings of members not reached this time are carried over and grow staler week by week. A count is a snapshot: it describes its day and goes stale as positions move.

member.name: T:SeatOfPower.Sim.Systems.Intel.XDateService
member.summary: X-date estimates (09 §5). Every estimator runs the Treasury's cash model forward from public data () many times, drawing what it doesn't know: the level of receipts (learned from the months booked so far, so the range narrows as data arrives), the strength of the April tax season (known once April is in), a drift in receipts as the economy changes, and daily noise. The quoted range is a pair of quantiles of the drawn dates. The Treasury's own estimate is narrower and shifted by its secretary's caution; the CBO-style estimate is unbiased and wider; banks' desks are noisier and some are alarmist, and alarming notes move markets.

member.name: T:SeatOfPower.Sim.Systems.Policy.BillEvaluator
member.summary: Turns a bill into a position, stakes and cost (06 §5), and scores it for an actor with preferences, salience and stakes. This is the default provision model; the politics system (05) builds bloc utility on top of it and may refine it.
member.remarks: Provision model: policies use their position and stakes (scaled by level); appropriations push the fiscal dimension towards dove (spending) or hawk (cuts) in proportion to size; debt-limit raises and suspensions are fiscally dovish and matter to the Treasury market; sweeteners have no position but touch the target's stakes.

member.name: M:SeatOfPower.Sim.Systems.Policy.BillEvaluator.Profile(SeatOfPower.Sim.Systems.Policy.BillProvision,SeatOfPower.Sim.Content.ContentDatabase)
member.summary: One provision's profile.

Scores a bill for an actor. Each provision's alignment is 100 − salience-weighted distance (−100..+100), weighted by the provision's share of the bill; stakes add Σ actorStake × provisionStake / 100. Policies listed in are reported as poison pills.
member.param: How much each dimension matters to the actor.
The bill (to map provisions to policies for poison pills).
Policies the actor will never accept (from red lines), or null.

member.name: T:SeatOfPower.Sim.Systems.Politics.DeadlineService
member.summary: Must-pass deadlines (12): politics.urgency follows the nearer of the debt-limit X-date and the end of government funding, as the public sees them, and while payments are missed or the government is shut down the leader takes daily approval damage and a share of the blame.
member.remarks: Urgency is a logistic of the days left: for the X-date, 50 at three weeks (the Treasury's latest early date, else the true date) and about 85 at ten days; for funding, 50 at ten days. Real deals land in the last days (2011: two days before the X-date, 2013: one day, 2023: nine days), and serious talks start a month or so out. Blame: in the 2013 and 2018–19 shutdowns the President lost 2–4 points while the side seen as demanding conditions took most of the blame; a missed payment has no precedent, so a month-long bond default costs about 8–10 points when the leader is mostly blamed.

member.summary: Parliamentary government (27 §7.1). Weekly, for each full country whose is parliamentary: how many seats would back the government in a confidence vote (), how much the opposition wants to bring it down (), and whether the opposition's leader tables a motion (dp.file_no_confidence). A tabled motion sets a flag that starts the country's no-confidence procedure (23 §7), whose stages hold the vote and, if the government falls, the mandate rounds and the endings.

member.name: T:SeatOfPower.Sim.Systems.Politics.IncidentReactions
member.summary: How politics reacts to 23's incidents (23 §6, 05 §7, §9, §10). When an incident is recorded: its target remembers it (tag {verb}_{targetKind}, magnitude from severity and legality), a contested or unlawful executed order goes to court, and norm-breaking acts move the regime indicators. When it becomes public: scandal rises, power centers that care about norms remember it, voter blocs that care about norms turn against the leader, the media frame it, and impeachment pressure is recomputed. A refused order that never leaks therefore costs far less than one on every front page.

member.name: T:SeatOfPower.Sim.Systems.Politics.LeadershipService
member.summary: Congressional leaders at a deadline (12): when the debt limit or government funding is close to running out and nothing that would fix it is moving, the lower chamber's leader decides (dp.leadership_bill) whether to wait, pass their own terms, a short extension or a clean bill. A bill they choose is drafted in their name and goes on the expedited route (no committee, one-day steps); it still needs both chambers, and then the leader's signature or a veto override.
member.remarks: Real precedents: the House majority passing its own terms before a deal (2011 "Cut, Cap and Balance", 2023 "Limit, Save, Grow"), short extensions under pressure (October 2021: $480 bn, two months), and continuing resolutions days before funding runs out (most years).

member.name: T:SeatOfPower.Sim.Systems.Politics.PoliticsSystem
member.summary: Internal politics (05): power centers, public opinion, unrest, the legislature, courts, regime drift, elections and threats to the player. Runs at . Daily: incidents, bills, court cases, elections due. Weekly (Mondays): opinion, power centers, regime drift, unrest, leverage, impeachment pressure, primary challenge, projections. Monthly: coup checks in autocracies.
member.remarks: Registers the 06 external effects pc_loyalty, bloc_approval and regime_indicator; the PowerCenterQuery and RegimeQuery services; PolicyHooks; the sweetener provision handler; the utility inputs actor.loyalty, actor.same_party, actor.satisfaction, actor.support, actor.grudge, leader.approval, politics.impeachment_pressure and politics.urgency; and the handlers of the politics decision points.

member.name: T:SeatOfPower.Sim.Systems.Politics.PoliticsVars

Country-level variables are defined in data/variables/politics.json (so content can read and modify them); per-power-center, per-voter-bloc and per-party variables are registered at run time by (content can't name them, but they have ledgers and history like any other variable).

member.name: T:SeatOfPower.Sim.Systems.Politics.UnrestModel
member.summary: Unrest as a threshold cascade (05 §5, Granovetter). Each voter bloc's potential protesters (at most of it) have thresholds spread normally around a mean set by the regime (fear raises it). One protests when grievance plus the pull of the movement's size exceeds their threshold, so participation stays near zero until grievance crosses a tipping point and then jumps: "passive until suddenly not". politics.unrest@country is the percent of the population protesting (5 is already mass protest). Package 20 extends this with movements and regime responses.

member.summary: Most of a bloc that will ever protest.

member.name: P:SeatOfPower.Sim.Systems.SimServices.RelationQuery
member.summary: Value of a relation metric (opinion, trust, threat, dependence) from one country to another, for relation conditions (registered by 08). Null until a package provides it.

member.name: P:SeatOfPower.Sim.Systems.SimServices.RelationShift
member.summary: Moves a relation (registered by 08): from one country to another, the metric (opinion, trust or threat), the change, a memory tag and the cause. Used by 07's Relation consequence. Null until 08 runs.

member.name: P:SeatOfPower.Sim.Systems.SimServices.ForeignReactors
member.summary: The foreign actors (country ids, in a stable order) who may react to an act in another country (08 §5), used by 07's reactions. Null until 08 runs: only the act's own country reacts.

member.name: P:SeatOfPower.Sim.Systems.SimServices.TariffResponse
member.summary: Called when a tariff takes effect (04): the target's leader decides how to answer (08: retaliate, negotiate or absorb). Arguments: imposer, target, rate (%). Returns true if handled; otherwise (or when null) 04's automatic retaliation runs.

member.name: P:SeatOfPower.Sim.Systems.SimServices.ForeignImpact
member.summary: How an act lands on a foreign actor (08 §5), replacing 07's domestic impact model for them.

member.name: P:SeatOfPower.Sim.Systems.SimServices.PowerCenterQuery
member.summary: Value of a power center metric (loyalty, satisfaction, support), for pc conditions (registered by 05). Null until a package provides it.

member.name: P:SeatOfPower.Sim.Systems.SimServices.RegimeQuery
member.summary: A country's current regime type (registered by 05 once regimes drift); defaults to the content value.

member.name: P:SeatOfPower.Sim.Systems.SimServices.OfficeHolder
member.summary: Who now holds the office a content character held at the start (registered by 09's advisors): the same id, a hired replacement, or null while the office is vacant. 23's chains use it so a newly hired official carries out orders.

member.name: P:SeatOfPower.Sim.Systems.SimServices.TraitQuery
member.summary: A character's current trait value (if traits can change at runtime); defaults to the content value.

member.name: P:SeatOfPower.Sim.Systems.SimServices.DecisionFactory

member.name: P:SeatOfPower.Sim.Systems.SimServices.EventAnnotator
